metadata.title: FAQ – Sendero Bike Trails
metadata.description: Answers on getting there, entry, climate, packing and booking for your mountain bike trip through the Colombian Andes.

faqPage.tripNote: Fitness, where you stay, your own bike and safety:

questions.question: How do I get to Pereira?
questions.answer: Pereira has its own airport, Matecaña (PEI), with connections via Bogotá or Medellín. The city’s bus terminal is also well connected to the rest of the country.

questions.question: Will someone pick me up?
questions.answer: Yes. The transfer from the airport or bus terminal in Pereira to Casa Tacay and back is included, as are all journeys on site.

questions.question: Can I extend my trip?
questions.answer: Yes. I'm happy to help with accommodation in Pereira and personal tips.

questions.question: Do I need a visa?
questions.answer: Not for stays of up to 90 days if you hold an EU passport. Your passport must be valid for at least 6 more months. Please check the rules for your nationality.

questions.question: Which vaccinations do I need?
questions.answer: Colombia is in the tropics. For our route, the yellow fever vaccination is especially recommended. Best talk to your doctor or a travel medicine specialist 6–8 weeks ahead.

questions.question: What insurance do I need?
questions.answer: Travel health insurance is mandatory and you take it out yourself – for example with HanseMerkur, SIGNAL IDUNA or BarmeniaGothaer (approx. €18–25).

questions.question: What's the climate like?
questions.answer: Tropical mountain climate: sun, mist and short showers take turns. Usually 16–24 °C – up on the páramo at 3,400 m it can get chilly, so pack a warm layer.

questions.question: Is there Wi-Fi and power?
questions.answer: There's Wi-Fi at Casa Tacay. Colombia uses 110 V with type A/B plugs – you can borrow adapters at the finca. For on the road I recommend an eSIM.

questions.question: What about laundry?
questions.answer: Laundry service at Casa Tacay is included, so you can travel light.

questions.question: What should I pack?
questions.answer: Comfortable riding clothes for a few days, a light rain jacket, a warm layer for the páramo, sun protection and sturdy shoes for evenings and outings.

questions.question: How does booking work?
questions.answer: You send me a non-binding request and I'll get back to you within 48 hours. When booking you pay a 20% deposit, the balance 30 days before departure – protected by a security certificate.

questions.question: Can I travel alone?
questions.answer: Absolutely. A single room is available for an extra €300.

questions.question: How do I pay on site?
questions.answer: VISA is accepted almost everywhere. For small purchases in the countryside I recommend some cash in pesos (COP).

aboutPage.title: About Julian — Sendero Bike Trails
aboutPage.description: Meet Julian, the Colombian-born, Berlin-based designer behind Sendero — a journey through Colombia's UNESCO coffee cultural landscape, inspired by Berlin's cycling culture and rooted in the Andes.
aboutPage.heading: Meet Julian
aboutPage.subtitle: From Berlin's cycling streets to the coffee-covered slopes of the Colombian Andes — the story behind Sendero.

berlin.heading: A Designer Shaped by Berlin
berlin.content: Julian has moved between two worlds — Berlin and Colombia — long before Sendero existed. Living in Berlin as a designer, he was pulled into its cycling culture: a city where the bike isn't a hobby but a way of moving through life, slowly enough to actually notice it. That rhythm — deliberate, unhurried, deeply attentive to place — became the lens through which he started to see his own roots differently.
berlin.imageAlt: Julian riding through Berlin's cycling culture

andes.heading: Rooted in the Colombian Andes
andes.content: Born in Colombia, Julian's family ties run deep into the mountains of the Coffee Region — the fincas, the cloud forests, the towns built into the folds of the Andes. It's a landscape he grew up close to but had never experienced the way Berlin taught him to see a place: on two wheels, at the pace of the land itself.
andes.imageAlt: The Colombian Andes coffee region, Julian's family roots

journey.heading: A Journey Built From Both Worlds
journey.content: Sendero is what happens when those two influences meet: Berlin's cycling culture and Colombia's UNESCO-listed coffee cultural landscape. Each trip is curated to move slowly through the depth of the Andes mountains — past working fincas, through cloud forest, and into towns shaped by a century of coffee — the way Julian first learned to experience a place, one pedal at a time.
journey.imageAlt: Cycling through the UNESCO coffee cultural landscape

scope.title: Scope
paragraphs: To the extent validly agreed, these terms form part of the package travel contract between the customer (hereinafter the “Traveler”) and sendero bike trails, owner Julian David Perez Rodriguez (hereinafter “sendero bike trails”). They supplement and specify the statutory provisions of §§ 651a–y of the German Civil Code (BGB) and Art. 250 and 252 of the Introductory Act to the German Civil Code (EGBGB).

They apply to all group trips advertised by sendero bike trails and to trips offered individually to private groups. Any deviating arrangements for private groups are stated expressly in the respective offer and in the trip confirmation.
sendero bike trails trips do not include flights to or from Colombia. The Traveler arranges their own travel to and from Colombia; it is not part of the package travel contract.
Before booking, the Traveler receives the standard information form for package travel required by law (Art. 250 § 2 EGBGB) and the pre-contractual information under Art. 250 § 3 EGBGB.

sections.title: 1. Conclusion of the package travel contract

clauses.text: The offer is based on the trip description on senderobiketrails.com, in sendero bike trails presentations or brochures, or on an individual offer, in each case together with any supplementary information available to the Traveler at the time of booking.

By booking (registering for a trip) via the booking form, by email or otherwise in text form, the Traveler makes sendero bike trails a binding offer to conclude the package travel contract. Anyone who books for additional participants is liable for their contractual obligations as for their own, provided they have expressly and separately assumed this obligation.
The contract is concluded when the Traveler receives sendero bike trails’ trip confirmation. The trip confirmation is sent on a durable medium (e.g., as a PDF by email).

If the trip confirmation differs from the booking, it constitutes a new offer by which sendero bike trails is bound for ten days. The contract is concluded on the basis of this new offer if sendero bike trails has pointed out the change and the Traveler accepts it within that period, either expressly or by paying the deposit.
Participants must be at least 18 years old. Minors may take part only by separate agreement and when accompanied by a parent or legal guardian.
There is no statutory right of withdrawal for package trips booked remotely (by phone, email or website) (§ 312(7) BGB). The statutory right to cancel under Section 5 remains unaffected.
Payments toward the trip price before the end of the trip are requested or accepted only upon handing over the insolvency protection certificate (Sicherungsschein, § 651r BGB) in text form.
Once the contract is concluded and the insolvency protection certificate has been received, a deposit of 20% of the trip price is due within 7 days.

The balance is due 30 days before departure. If the trip is still subject to the minimum number of participants (Section 8.1), the balance only becomes due once sendero bike trails can no longer cancel the trip for this reason or has confirmed that it will go ahead.
For bookings made within 30 days of departure, the full trip price is due immediately upon receipt of the insolvency protection certificate.
Payments are made by bank transfer to the account stated on the invoice or via a payment link provided by sendero bike trails. The Traveler bears any bank fees for international transfers.

If the Traveler fails to pay the deposit or balance on time despite having received the insolvency protection certificate, sendero bike trails may, after a reminder setting a deadline, withdraw from the contract and claim compensation in accordance with Section 5.3, unless there is a travel defect that would entitle the Traveler to withdraw.
Without full payment, there is no entitlement to travel documents or travel services.

The scope of services is set out in the trip confirmation together with the trip description valid at the time of booking and the pre-contractual information. Details of stages, distances, elevation gain and trail character are approximate.
Local service providers (e.g., accommodations, transport companies, local guides) are not authorized to make any promises that deviate from the confirmed contract.

Changes to individual travel services after the contract is concluded that sendero bike trails has not brought about in bad faith are permitted, provided they are insignificant and do not affect the overall character of the trip. These include in particular adjustments to the route, daily stages or the order of the program due to weather, trail and road conditions, the security situation or the fitness of the group, replacing an accommodation with an equivalent one, and assigning a different qualified guide. sendero bike trails informs the Traveler of any such changes clearly and comprehensibly on a durable medium before departure.

In the event of a significant change to an essential travel service, the Traveler may, within a reasonable period set by sendero bike trails, accept the change, withdraw from the contract free of charge, or choose an alternative trip if one is offered. If the Traveler does not respond in time, the change is deemed accepted. The notification will point this out.
Warranty claims remain unaffected. If the changed trip or alternative trip is not of equivalent value, the trip price is reduced in accordance with § 651m BGB.
sendero bike trails waives the right to increase the trip price after the contract is concluded. The trip price confirmed at booking is a fixed price.

sections.title: 5. Cancellation by the Traveler before departure, substitute traveler

clauses.text: The Traveler may withdraw from the contract at any time before departure. The cancellation must be declared to sendero bike trails using the contact details below, preferably in text form (email). The date it is received by sendero bike trails is decisive.

If the Traveler cancels or does not start the trip, sendero bike trails loses its claim to the trip price and may instead claim reasonable compensation. This does not apply if sendero bike trails is responsible for the cancellation, or if unavoidable and extraordinary circumstances occur at or near the destination that significantly affect the performance of the trip (e.g., a travel warning issued by the German Federal Foreign Office for the region, natural disasters, serious unrest).

Taking into account saved expenses and the usual possibility of using the travel services otherwise, the compensation is set at the following flat rates (per person, as a percentage of the trip price):

table.label: on the day of departure, or no-show

clauses.text: The Traveler remains free to prove that sendero bike trails has incurred no loss or a significantly lower loss. Instead of the flat rate, sendero bike trails may claim higher compensation calculated on an individual basis if it can prove significantly higher expenses; in that case it must quantify and justify the amount specifically.
If sendero bike trails has to refund payments as a result of the cancellation, the refund is made without undue delay and no later than 14 days after the cancellation.
Taking out trip cancellation and trip interruption insurance is strongly recommended (see Section 12).

Up to 7 days before departure, the Traveler may declare on a durable medium that a substitute will take part in their place (§ 651e BGB). sendero bike trails may object if the substitute does not meet the participation requirements under Section 9. The Traveler and the substitute are jointly and severally liable for the trip price and any additional costs actually incurred; sendero bike trails will provide evidence of these.

There is no entitlement to change the travel date, itinerary, accommodation or scope of services after the contract is concluded (rebooking). This does not apply to rebookings that become necessary because the pre-contractual information was incomplete or incorrect; these are free of charge.

If, at the Traveler’s request, sendero bike trails nevertheless rebooks the trip to a different date up to the 35th day before departure, a rebooking fee of €50 per person is charged, plus any additional costs from service providers. From the 34th day before departure onward, rebooking is only possible by cancelling under the terms of Section 5.3 and making a new booking.

If the Traveler does not use individual services that were duly offered, for reasons for which the Traveler is responsible (e.g., early departure, skipping stages, exclusion under Section 9.5), there is no entitlement to a partial refund. sendero bike trails will try to obtain a refund of saved expenses from the service providers, except for entirely insignificant services.

sections.title: 8. Cancellation and termination by sendero bike trails

clauses.text: sendero bike trails may withdraw from the contract if the minimum number of participants stated in the trip description and the trip confirmation is not reached. Unless stated otherwise there, the minimum is 4 Travelers. The cancellation must be declared no later than 30 days before departure. If it becomes clear earlier that the number will not be reached, sendero bike trails will inform the Traveler without undue delay. Payments made are refunded within 14 days. Alternatively, sendero bike trails may offer to run the trip at an adjusted price or offer an alternative trip; the Traveler is not obliged to accept.

If sendero bike trails is prevented from performing the trip by such circumstances (e.g., a travel warning, serious security incidents, natural events, failure of the region’s infrastructure), sendero bike trails may withdraw before departure. The cancellation is declared without undue delay once sendero bike trails becomes aware of the circumstances; payments are refunded within 14 days.

sendero bike trails may terminate the contract without notice if, despite a warning, the Traveler persistently disrupts the trip, repeatedly or grossly disregards the tour leader’s safety instructions, or otherwise acts in breach of contract to such an extent that immediate termination is justified. In that case, sendero bike trails retains its claim to the trip price, less saved expenses and any benefits obtained. The Traveler bears any additional costs of the return journey.

sections.title: 9. Special conditions for guided mountain bike tours

clauses.text: Each trip description assigns the trip to one of three levels – Relaxed, Flowy or Technical – and sets out the daily distances, elevation gain and altitude (in places above 2,500 m) involved. The trails ridden go no higher than grade S2 on the Singletrail Scale. Before booking, the Traveler checks on their own responsibility whether they meet these requirements and, if in doubt, consults sendero bike trails.

By booking, the Traveler confirms that they are fit enough for the trip booked. Before departure, they complete a participant questionnaire covering riding ability, relevant pre-existing conditions, allergies, medication and an emergency contact. A medical check-up before the trip is recommended for anyone with pre-existing conditions or after a longer break from training. If the Traveler’s health changes significantly after booking, they inform sendero bike trails without undue delay.

Helmets are mandatory on all rides. Gloves and suitable footwear are mandatory; protective gear is recommended or, where stated in the trip description, required. Without a helmet, the Traveler cannot take part in the stage concerned.

Guides working for sendero bike trails and its local partners are entitled, for safety reasons, to change routes, shorten sections, bypass trails, call breaks or have riders push their bikes on certain passages. Their instructions on riding style, spacing within the group and behavior in road traffic must be followed. Colombian traffic rules apply on public roads.

If, in the tour leader’s judgment, a Traveler is visibly overstretched, ill, injured, under the influence of alcohol or without the required equipment, they may be excluded from individual stages for their own safety and that of the group. In such cases, sendero bike trails will, where possible, offer a ride in the support vehicle to the day’s destination. Refunds are only made in accordance with Section 7.

Off-road mountain biking involves risks typical of the sport (e.g., falls, changing surfaces, weather, animals, oncoming traffic on trails). The Traveler rides within their own ability and chooses their own speed and line. This provision does not limit sendero bike trails’ liability for its own breaches of duty, in particular its duties of organization and supervision.

Unless stated otherwise in the trip description, the trip price includes the use of a full-suspension mountain bike in a frame size agreed with the Traveler, including maintenance during the trip. The bikes are provided by sendero bike trails’ local partner in Colombia. The bike is handed over at the start of the trip in good working order, with a short handover record. By arrangement, the Traveler may bring their own pedals and saddle.

The Traveler treats the rental bike with care, reports any damage or defects to the guide without undue delay, and secures the bike during breaks as the guide instructs. Normal wear and tear is not charged to the Traveler.

For damage or loss beyond normal wear and tear, the Traveler is liable for the full repair costs or current value in cases of intent or gross negligence. In cases of slight negligence, liability is limited to €300 per incident. Damage caused by falls typical of the sport during proper use is not considered negligent.

Instead of the rental bike, the Traveler may bring their own mountain bike. This must be stated when booking or no later than 30 days before departure. The trip price is only reduced if a reduction is stated in the trip description. The bike must be suitable for the advertised trails and in good working order; the tour leader may refuse a bike that is not roadworthy or safe to ride and, where available, provide a rental bike.

Bringing their own bike is at the Traveler’s own risk. Transport, packing and insurance on the way to and from Colombia, as well as damage, loss or theft during the trip, are the Traveler’s responsibility, unless sendero bike trails is responsible for a breach of duty. Minor repairs by the support team are carried out without warranty; spare parts are charged at cost. Bike or baggage insurance is recommended.

Once payment has been made in full, the travel documents (meeting point, schedule, emergency contacts) are usually sent by email 14 days before departure. If the Traveler does not receive them in time, they inform sendero bike trails.

The Traveler is responsible for arriving on time at the meeting point or airport transfer stated in the trip confirmation (e.g., Pereira). sendero bike trails recommends booking flights only once the trip has been confirmed (Section 8.1) or on a flexible fare. If the Traveler arrives late, they bear the additional costs of a separate transfer; sendero bike trails is not liable for the cost of flights the Traveler has booked.

The Traveler must report any travel defect without undue delay to the tour leader on site or, if the tour leader cannot be reached, directly to sendero bike trails, and request a remedy. If the Traveler culpably fails to do so and sendero bike trails was therefore unable to remedy the defect, the Traveler has no claim to a price reduction (§ 651m BGB) or damages (§ 651n BGB) in that respect. The tour leader is not authorized to acknowledge claims.

If the Traveler wishes to terminate the contract because of a significant defect (§ 651l BGB), they must first give sendero bike trails a reasonable period to remedy it, unless a remedy is impossible, is refused, or is needed immediately.

Damage to or loss of baggage and bikes during air travel must be reported to the airline on the spot without undue delay using a Property Irregularity Report (P.I.R.) – within 7 days for damage and within 21 days for delay.
The trip price does not include any insurance for the Traveler.

Every Traveler must take out international travel health insurance that covers medical treatment in Colombia, search and rescue, and medically appropriate repatriation to Germany, and that does not exclude cycling/mountain biking. Proof (name of insurer, policy number, emergency number) must be submitted with the participant questionnaire no later than 14 days before departure. Without proof, sendero bike trails may refuse participation in the stages; Section 7 applies accordingly.
sendero bike trails strongly recommends trip cancellation and trip interruption insurance, personal accident and liability insurance that covers cycling abroad, and baggage or bike insurance.
sendero bike trails holds tour operator liability insurance for its activities as a tour operator.

sendero bike trails’ contractual liability for damage that is not bodily injury and was not caused culpably is limited to three times the trip price (§ 651p(1) BGB). Where international conventions or provisions based on them limit or exclude the liability of a service provider for a travel service, sendero bike trails may also rely on them (§ 651p(2) BGB).

sendero bike trails is not liable for performance failures, personal injury or property damage in connection with services that are merely arranged as third-party services (e.g., excursions booked locally, coffee tours, hot springs, paragliding), provided these are expressly identified as third-party services, naming the contracting party, in the trip description and trip confirmation. This does not apply where a breach of sendero bike trails’ duties to inform, advise or organize was the cause.
sendero bike trails is not liable for activities the Traveler undertakes independently outside the program during the trip (e.g., rides in their free time, exploring on their own).
Liability for damage resulting from injury to life, body or health, and for damage caused intentionally or through gross negligence, remains unlimited.

Before the contract is concluded, sendero bike trails provides information on the general passport and visa requirements for Colombia and on health formalities, and on any changes to them before departure. This information applies to citizens of the EU, Switzerland and Liechtenstein without special circumstances (e.g., dual citizenship, statelessness).

The Traveler is responsible for obtaining and carrying their travel documents (a passport with sufficient validity and, where applicable, the Check-MIG online entry form), for any recommended or required vaccinations, and for complying with customs and currency regulations. Any disadvantages resulting from failure to do so are borne by the Traveler, unless sendero bike trails culpably failed to inform them, or informed them inadequately or incorrectly.

The German Federal Foreign Office publishes current travel, safety and medical advice (auswaertiges-amt.de). sendero bike trails recommends seeing a travel medicine specialist before the trip, including about altitude.

On some trips, a photographer commissioned by sendero bike trails accompanies the group at selected points along the route. Images in which the Traveler can be recognized are used for the website, social media or print only with the Traveler’s separate consent, which is requested with the participant questionnaire and can be withdrawn at any time with effect for the future. Consent is not a condition of participation.
Travelers receive the photos of their trip for private, non-commercial use. Copyright remains with the photographer or with sendero bike trails.

sendero bike trails processes the Traveler’s personal data to perform the contract (Art. 6(1)(b) GDPR) and passes it on only to the service providers in Colombia needed for the trip (e.g., accommodations, the local partner for guiding and transport). Health information from the participant questionnaire is processed only with express consent (Art. 9(2)(a) GDPR), solely for the safe running of the trip and for emergencies, and is deleted no later than 3 months after the end of the trip. Details can be found in the privacy policy on senderobiketrails.com.

Claims under § 651i(3) BGB must be asserted against sendero bike trails using the contact details below, preferably in text form. Under § 651j BGB, claims become time-barred two years after the contractually agreed end of the trip.
Claims may not be assigned to third parties who are not participants in the trip.
sendero bike trails does not take part in dispute resolution proceedings before a consumer arbitration board and is not obliged to do so (§ 36 VSBG).
The contractual relationship is governed exclusively by German law, even where the travel services are provided in Colombia.

The Traveler may only sue sendero bike trails at its registered place of business (Berlin). For claims brought by sendero bike trails against the Traveler, the Traveler’s place of residence is decisive. For claims against merchants, legal entities and Travelers who have no residence or habitual abode in Germany, or whose residence is unknown, Berlin is agreed as the place of jurisdiction.

These provisions do not apply insofar as mandatory provisions of international agreements, or of the EU member state of which the Traveler is a national, are more favorable to the Traveler. For Travelers resident in Switzerland, the mandatory consumer protection provisions of their country of residence apply.
If individual provisions are invalid, this does not affect the validity of the rest of the travel contract.

seo.title: Mountain Bike Trip Colombia – Old Trails Through the Andes
seo.description: Small groups, ancient trails and a coffee finca as your home: a mountain bike trip through Colombia's Andes, personally guided. From €3,290.

hero.title: Between coffee and clouds.
hero.text: Small groups, ancient trails and a coffee finca as your home – right in the heart of Colombia's Andes.

region.heading: Mountains written by people.
paragraphs: In 2011, UNESCO declared these Andean slopes a World Heritage Site – not as untouched wilderness, but as a cultural landscape: mountains shaped by generations of people, terrace by terrace, trail by trail.

Long before the first coffee bush, this was Quimbaya country. Their goldsmiths made figures so fine they now fill display cases in Bogotá and Madrid. In the 19th century, settlers from Antioquia cut mule trails through the cloud forest and built villages of bamboo and mud on slopes that are really too steep for them. Many of those paths are still here.

A mountain bike is the right pace for this land: slow enough for a chat over a fence, a break beneath wax palms, a look into a roadside workshop – and fast enough to climb, in a single week, from warm bamboo valleys to the páramo at 3,400 meters.
region.imageAlt: An old trail on a steep Andean slope

itinerary.heading: Day by day
itinerary.intro: Around 20 km a day, with time for breaks, conversations and views. Back at Casa Tacay every evening.

arrival.title: Arrival
arrival.text: After you land at Matecaña Airport or arrive at Pereira's bus terminal, we take you to Casa Tacay. There's time to settle in, meet the group, set up the bikes and go over the most important notes for the trip. At our first dinner together we raise a glass to the days ahead.

tigre.title: Sendero del Tigre
tigre.text: To acclimatize, we ride bamboo-lined paths and through fruit orchards to Finca Ganday. There we discover the variety of Colombian crops and enjoy a traditional caldo made with ingredients from the finca – following a recipe from the mountains and the Amazon.

cafe.title: Sendero del Café
cafe.text: On quiet country roads we ride through the UNESCO Coffee Cultural Landscape – past plantations, small pueblos and colorful houses. Included: a coffee and art workshop with our hosts.

agua.title: Sendero del Agua
agua.text: We follow winding paths along rivers and through dense cloud forest around La Florida. Along the way we cross bridges, pass waterfalls and, with a bit of luck, meet animals big and small. Lunch is a regional mountain meal with a view.

cacao.title: Sendero del Cacao
cacao.text: Get to know cacao like you've never tasted it: from the fruit on the tree through fermentation to finished chocolate. You roast your own nibs and take your creation home. The evening ends with music at Casa Tacay.

volcan.title: Sendero del Volcán
volcan.text: Between wax palms, Colombia's national tree, and volcano panoramas, this is one of the most spectacular rides of the trip. In the afternoon we stop in Salento – time to stroll, browse and take the place in.

oro.title: Sendero del Oro
oro.text: Today we combine riding with history. After visiting the Gold Museum in Armenia, we ride quiet back roads and old connecting paths through the land of the Quimbaya and discover the origins of the region's culture.

paramo.title: Sendero del Páramo
paramo.text: To close, one of the most impressive rides of the trip awaits: up to 3,400 meters, past lagoons, high plateaus and plants found nowhere else. We celebrate the last evening together with an Andean dinner at Casa Tacay.

departure.title: Departure
departure.text: After a last breakfast together, it's time to say goodbye. Check-out is at 11 am, then our driver takes you to the airport or bus terminal.

faq.heading: Questions about the trip

items.question: Is this trip for me?
paragraphs: If you enjoy being active, yes. You should be able to sit comfortably in the saddle for a few hours – no pressure to perform, but up for small challenges. You don't need to be a mountain bike pro: if you ride confidently and feel at ease on gravel, forest tracks and unpaved trails, you have everything you need.

The trip is made for people who are after landscapes and encounters as much as kilometers, who enjoy a small group, and who'd rather come home to one familiar place each evening than check into a new hotel. If you're chasing personal bests and long trail descents, or want to sleep somewhere new every night, another trip will make you happier.

items.question: Where do I stay during the trip?
paragraphs: At Casa Tacay, a family home in the mountains near Pereira. Every riding day starts here and ends here too: you unpack once and only pack again when you leave.
Every room has its own bathroom, and there is Wi-Fi in the house. If you travel alone and want a single room, it costs an extra €300.

items.question: Can I bring my own bike?
paragraphs: Yes. If you'd rather ride your own, we'll work out the best way to get it to Pereira when you send your request. Our mechanic checks it before the first ride and keeps it in shape for the whole trip.
If you don't bring one, you ride a high-quality full-suspension mountain bike in your size, with helmet and gear included. You're welcome to bring your own pedals and saddle.

items.question: Can I do this trip privately?
paragraphs: Yes. For friends, family or your club, I'll plan your own trip – on your dates and at your pace. We shape the length, routes and program together.

items.question: Can I ride all year round?
paragraphs: Yes. Close to the equator, the Andes have no winter: the climate stays mild all year, usually between 16 and 24 °C. Drier and wetter months take turns, but we ride in all of them. Group trips run in March, April and May 2027; private trips are possible all year.
Short showers are part of the mountain climate and usually pass quickly. Pack a light rain jacket; in heavy rain we adjust the route or set off a little later.

items.question: How safe is the trip?
paragraphs: The mountains around Pereira are among the most stable regions in Colombia. We move within a network of partners, families and guides I know personally. I guide every trip myself, together with my local partner, a certified bike guide and mechanic, and a support vehicle that comes along on every ride.

There's a safety briefing on day one. Our guides are trained in first aid, we follow an emergency protocol and carry satellite communication. And if a ride is ever too much, we adjust the route or you hop into the support vehicle. Nobody gets left behind.
